8 22 58] In the Mahabharata [Karna-vadha-parva]

I will surely defeat all the gathered Pandavas today. 58
Duryodhana said:
I will do all this exactly as you think best, O Karna.
The chariots, equipped with quivers and horses, will follow you, O son of a charioteer <note>original: "sutaja", an epithet for Karna</note>. 59
Let the carts carry your iron arrows feathered with vulture plumes.

<column-break/>

We and all the kings shall follow you, O Karna. 60
Sanjaya said:
Having spoken thus, O Great King, your powerful son,
the King <note>Duryodhana</note>, approached the King of Madra <note>Shalya</note> and spoke these words. 61

->Thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the Karna-parva of the glorious Mahabharata. 22<-

---

## 23

Sanjaya said:
Your son, O Great King, approached the King of Madra
<column-break/>
with humility and spoke these words out of affection. 1
O you who are devoted to truth, O highly fortunate one, O increaser of the grief of your enemies.

---

<summary>Duryodhana agrees to Karna's battle preparations and approaches Shalya, the King of Madra, to request his assistance. This transition marks the end of chapter 22 and the beginning of chapter 23 in the Karna-parva.</summary>
